The generic projection documentation is partly updated, but its configuration guidance and two CLI guarantees do not match the shipped behavior.

1. **F1 — blocking, issue-impact (high):** The canonical configuration reference omits `[projection.<name>]`, and its advertised “Full annotated example with all options” also has no projection example. Adopters cannot discover how to declare `kind`, `mode`, `target`, `style`, or optional region markers in the canonical configuration location. Add a `[projection.<name>]` section to [docs/reference/configuration.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/configuration.md:32) and an annotated example to `docs/reference/example-config.toml`, covering project-scoped kinds, both modes/styles, defaults, and `jit project render`.

2. **F2 — blocking, issue-impact (medium):** [docs/reference/cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3100) says `id-anchor` renders rows from “any kind,” but the implementation rejects non-project-scoped kinds with `NotProjectScoped`. Qualify this as project-scoped addressable kinds and state that issue-scoped kinds cannot be projected.

3. **F3 — blocking, issue-impact (medium):** [docs/reference/cli-commands.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/cli-commands.md:3103) promises that an error means “nothing is written.” When rendering all projections, the command writes them sequentially, so a later failure can leave earlier projections updated. Document the per-projection atomicity and possible earlier writes, or make the command batch-atomic before retaining this guarantee.

Total findings: 3
